Hi team,

Quick context: Santorini (Sara Goldman) is the lead for a $1.2M ARR opportunity (pilot -> enterprise conversion). Customer has approval to sign if we agree to three non-standard items in their final commercial: 1) MFN across comparable feature tiers, 2) a benchmark clause tying price to a competitor metric, and 3) a 12-month exclusivity on their integration vertical (they want a product-level exclusivity ask across our "Conductor" integration). They are also requesting a 25% up-front discount for year one.

I've attached the latest redline (Santorini_Redline_v3.pdf) and a short commercial impact sheet. Key numbers: ACV $1.2M, initial TCV year1 $900k (after their requested 25% off), renewal expected year2 at list if no MFN applies.

Why I think escalation is needed: MFN + benchmark together effectively give them price parity that could cascade into future enterprise marketplace deals; exclusivity at product-level for 12 months removes runway for other partners in that vertical. They are strategic (pilot with high visibility) but these clauses are outside deal desk guardrails.

Requested: executive guidance on whether we can accept any of these items and if so, under what constraints. If not, direction on a counter-proposal I should send today.

Attachments: Santorini_Redline_v3.pdf (proposed contract), commercial_summary.xlsx

Thanks,
Mina Haddad

Mina — thanks for the summary and attachments. TL;DR: high risk.

Notes from Deal Desk:
- Financial impact: a straight 25% concession pushes initial year margin from ~36% to ~24% before any infra or premium support add-ons.
- MFN: deal desk policy is to decline enterprise-wide MFN. We can consider limited, time-bound MFN scoped to a narrowly defined product bundle and only for published, public offers (no private marketplace/vendor exceptions).
- Benchmark clause: acceptable only if it references a public, objectively measurable metric (e.g., avg. token price on X) and excludes in-development features. We should avoid tieing future price changes to competitor private negotiations.
- Exclusivity: we can accept a short, narrow exclusive period for a specific integration with a 90-day maximum and defined performance milestones. 12 months is not acceptable.

Recommended counter: 20% max discount for Y1, MFN limited to 6 months and to published list prices only, benchmark clause rewritten to a non-price performance benchmark, exclusivity 90 days and only for the named "Conductor" integration, and a sunset clause if usage thresholds aren't met.

If you want to escalate price beyond 20% or exclusivity >90 days, will need VP approval.

-Marissa
Sr. Deal Desk Manager

Looping in a few quick legal points on the redline:
- MFN: If we accept any MFN language it must be tightly scoped (product IDs, feature flags) and include an express carve-out for marketplace and channel partner pricing. Add an anti-aggregation clause so they cannot combine separate offerings to claim MFN.
- Benchmark: rewrite to be a measurement of service level or availability (99.9% uptime-based credits) rather than competitor pricing. If they insist on pricing-based benchmarking, require a defined public index and audit rights limited to metadata (no data transfer).
- Exclusivity: legal will accept a limited commercial exclusivity tied to specific SKUs and explicitly excluding resellers/marketplaces. Add termination-on-breach language and a performance milestone (e.g., $X usage in 90 days) to keep it short.
- Discounts: any concession >20% must be documented with approval from sales leadership and finance; require a make-whole clause on renewals if benchmarks are met.

I marked up the attached pdf with inline changes (see Santorini_Redline_v3.pdf). Happy to take a call with Mina and the customer legal team if needed.

Evelyn Hart
Head of Legal

Thanks for the signals. Decision guidance:
- Discount: approved up to 20% for Y1 only. Beyond that requires CFO sign-off.
- MFN: can accept a time-limited MFN of up to 9 months but must be limited to a specific published product bundle and exclude marketplace/channel pricing. Add anti-aggregation and a cap on any retroactive application.
- Benchmark: prefer to limit to operational/service-level benchmarks (uptime, latency) rather than price; if customer insists on price benchmark, it must reference a public index and include mutual audit constraints.
- Exclusivity: not approved at product-level for 12 months. We can offer a 90-day narrowly scoped exclusivity for the Conductor integration only, contingent on performance milestones (50% of pilot seats activated within 60 days) and an early-termination make-whole if thresholds aren't met.

Conditional approval: If Mina can get Santorini to accept our counter (20% Y1 discount, 90-day Conductor exclusivity, MFN 9 months scoped to published list, and legal addendum with carve-outs) I approve moving forward. If Santorini refuses, we should walk.

-Rishi
VP, Sales
